names.official: Income tax (first category, second category, global complementary and additional taxes, with the mining royalty)

taxes.base: Profits of businesses (first category tax), wages (second category), the total annual income of individuals (global complementary) and income of non-residents from Chile (additional tax).
taxes.payer: Companies, individuals and non-residents; large mining companies also pay the royalty.

rate.headline: Companies 27%; individuals 0%–40%
details: First category tax: 27% of profits under the general regime, lower for small firms.
Individuals: progressive from 0% (exempt up to 13.5 annual tax units) to 40%, withheld monthly on wages and settled in the annual return.
Non-residents: additional tax, generally 35% of the income.
Mining: DIPRES credits the mining royalty of Law 21,591, in force since 2024, for part of the rise in revenue.

instruments.explanation: The largest tax. It is collected mostly through monthly payments on account: provisional payments of firms (17.3 trillion pesos) and monthly declared payments (8.7 trillion); the annual return settles the difference. DIPRES separately reports 5.3 trillion pesos of taxes from the ten largest private copper mining companies (up 47% in real terms, credited to the new royalty and the copper price); it does not say in which tax lines they fall.
exceptions: One core: the report does not split the revenue between the four taxes of the income tax law.

names.official: Value-added tax (Impuesto al Valor Agregado, IVA)

taxes.base: Sales of goods and services and imports, with credit for the VAT paid on inputs.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and remit the balance; customs collects it on imports.

rate.headline: 19% on most supplies
details: Exports are zero-rated; some services, such as health and education, are exempt.

instruments.explanation: Nearly half of the net central taxes. The net figure follows from 44.2 trillion pesos of VAT declared, less refunds of 15.2 trillion (mostly to exporters) and a special credit of 0.4 for construction firms.

taxes.base: Gasoline and diesel, per cubic metre, on first sale or import.
taxes.payer: Refiners and importers; passed on at the pump.

rate.headline: 6 UTM/m³ gasoline, 1.5 UTM/m³ diesel, plus a variable part
details: The base amounts are in monthly tax units (UTM). Law 20,493 adds a variable component (the price stabilisation mechanism, MEPCO) that can raise or lower the tax.
DIPRES reports the variable part for gasoline moving from −0.072 UTM/m³ in December 2024 to +0.626 in December 2025, and for diesel from −0.194 to +0.520.

instruments.explanation: The tax moves with the oil price: fuel revenue rose 10.7% in real terms in 2025 as the variable component turned from a rebate to a charge.
exceptions: Firms that pay VAT can recover part of the tax as VAT credit.

taxes.base: Cigarettes, cigars and other manufactured tobacco.
taxes.payer: Manufacturers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Cigarettes: 30% of the retail price plus a specific amount
details: 0.0010304240 monthly tax units per cigarette plus 30% of the retail price per pack, the rates set by Law 20,780 from October 2014 (SII); later changes not checked.

instruments.explanation: Revenue fell 5.7% in real terms in 2025.

names.native: Derechos de extracción, Ley de Pesca

taxes.base: The right to extract fish under the General Fisheries and Aquaculture Act; holders of transferable fishing licences pay a specific tax each July on the tonnes they may extract.

rate.headline: Per tonne of licensed catch, by statute
details: The unit value is set each year by ministerial resolution.

instruments.explanation: A small levy on the resource that fishing firms use. The report calls the line "Der. de Extracción Ley de Pesca" and does not name the provision; the specific tax on licences (Art. 43 ter, Law 20,657) is the most likely content, which is an inference.

taxes.base: Documents that record legal acts, above all credit operations (loans, bills and notes), charged by the months of the credit’s term.
taxes.payer: The debtor or the party to the document.

rate.headline: A percentage per month of credit term, capped
details: Fixed amounts apply to some other documents.

instruments.explanation: Known in the budget as the tax on legal acts.

taxes.base: The CIF value of imported goods.

rate.headline: 6% general rate; 0.71% effective
details: Trade agreements remove or cut the duty for partner countries; the effective rate on all imports was 0.71% at the end of 2024.

instruments.explanation: A uniform tariff since 2003, made small in practice by trade agreements.
exceptions: Some farm goods carry specific duties.

names.official: Social security contributions recorded by the central government (imposiciones previsionales)

taxes.base: Wages of workers who contribute to public social security bodies, such as the health fund FONASA and the public pension institutions.
taxes.payer: Workers and, for some schemes, their employers.

rate.headline: Health contribution 7% of taxable pay
details: Pension contributions to public schemes follow each scheme’s rules. Contributions to private pension managers are not part of this revenue.

instruments.explanation: The only compulsory contributions that appear in the government accounts. DIPRES says they grew 22.4% in December 2025 as fewer workers used the sick-leave subsidy.

taxes.base: The fiscal assessment (avalúo fiscal) of land and buildings, revalued periodically by the SII.

rate.headline: About 1% of the assessment, set by decree
details: The rates are fixed by supreme decree under Law 17,235; homes below a threshold are exempt.

instruments.explanation: The tax is set and collected nationally, and the money goes to municipalities. By law 60% of the revenue (65% for Santiago, Providencia, Las Condes and Vitacura) is pooled in the Common Municipal Fund and redistributed; each municipality keeps the rest.

names.official: Municipal commercial licences and vehicle circulation permits
names.native: Patentes municipales y permisos de circulación

taxes.base: Licences: every lucrative activity exercised in the commune, charged on the capital of the business. Permits: the annual permit to drive a vehicle, charged by vehicle type.

rate.headline: By capital (licences) and by vehicle (permits)
details: Set in monthly tax units by the Municipal Revenue Law. Two charges in one core: the OECD reports them together.

instruments.explanation: Two municipal charges that the OECD does not separate. 62.5% of the permit revenue is pooled in the Common Municipal Fund; commercial licences are pooled only for the four richest communes.
